Mifflin County Courthouse

The Mifflin County Court of Common Pleas stands AKA Mifflin County Courthouse as a cornerstone of justice in central Pennsylvania, serving the residents of Mifflin County with distinction and dedication. Located in the historic courthouse at 20 North Wayne Street in Lewistown, this institution plays a vital role in maintaining the rule of law and providing essential judicial services to the community.

About the Court Administrator's Office

The Court Administrator's Office serves as the administrative backbone of the Mifflin County judicial system. This office oversees crucial support functions that ensure the smooth operation of both the Common Pleas Court and the Minor Judiciary. Their responsibilities encompass a wide range of duties, including juror management, fiscal oversight, personnel administration, strategic planning, data processing, caseflow management, and public information services.

wha is the Court Leadership and Structure for Mifflin County Courthouse

Under the leadership of President Judge Aaron L. Gingrich and Judge Jonathan W. Reed, the court maintains a robust organizational structure that promotes efficiency and accessibility. The judicial leadership works in tandem with Court Administrator Christine Stuck and Deputy Court Administrator Rachel Burchfield to ensure seamless operations across all departments.

What is the Location for Mifflin County Courthouse

Situated in downtown Lewistown, the courthouse offers convenient access to all residents of Mifflin County. Visitors can find the Court Administrator's Office on the third floor, accessible via elevator from the main lobby. The office's strategic location allows for easy coordination between various judicial departments and provides straightforward access for the public.

what are the Court Services and Operations for Mifflin County Courthouse

what are Operating Hours and Schedule for Mifflin County Courthouse

The court maintains regular business hours designed to serve the public effectively:

  • Morning hours: 8:00 AM to 12:00 PM
  • Afternoon hours: 12:45 PM to 4:00 PM
  • Monday through Friday (excluding holidays)

What are the Departments and Divisions for Mifflin County Courthouse

The court system encompasses several key departments:

  • Magisterial District Judges Office
  • Probation and Parole Department
  • Domestic Relations Section
  • Case Coordination Department
  • Digital Court Recording Services

Programs and Special Services at Mifflin County Courthouse

The court offers various specialized services and programs designed to meet the diverse needs of the community. These include digital recording systems for accurate court documentation, comprehensive jury services, and various support programs for court users.

What are Judicial Leadership and Staff at Mifflin County Courthouse

President Judge and Judiciary

The Honorable Aaron L. Gingrich serves as President Judge, working alongside Judge Jonathan W. Reed to oversee judicial proceedings and maintain the highest standards of justice. Their combined experience and dedication ensure fair and efficient administration of justice throughout the county.

Administrative Personnel

The court's administrative team includes:

  • Christine Stuck – Court Administrator
  • Rachel Burchfield – Deputy Court Administrator
  • Jan Smith – Court Reporter

Support Staff and Services

A dedicated team of case coordinators and digital court recorders supports daily operations:

  • Angela Crisswell
  • Jennifer Sheaffer
  • Janette Ouedraogo

how to Access Public Services and Resources at Mifflin County Courthouse

Jury Services and Management

The court provides comprehensive jury management services through its eJury system, making it convenient for citizens to fulfill their civic duty. This modern approach to jury administration helps streamline the selection and management process.

Court Records Access

Public access to court records is facilitated through various channels, ensuring transparency while maintaining necessary security protocols. The court strives to balance public access with privacy considerations in accordance with state and federal regulations.

Americans with Disabilities Act Compliance

The courthouse maintains strict compliance with ADA requirements, ensuring all visitors have equal access to justice. The court's Title II ADA policy demonstrates its commitment to serving all members of the community, regardless of physical abilities.

What are Special Programs and Initiatives at Mifflin County Courthouse

Human Trafficking Prevention

The court maintains a strong stance against human trafficking, providing resources and information in both English and Spanish. This initiative demonstrates the court's commitment to addressing critical social issues affecting the community.

Digital Recording Systems

Implementation of advanced digital recording technology ensures accurate documentation of court proceedings. This system enhances transparency and maintains precise records of all court activities.

Community Outreach

The court actively engages with the community through various outreach programs and educational initiatives, fostering better understanding of the judicial system among residents.

Conclusion

The Mifflin County Court of Common Pleas represents a modern, efficient judicial institution dedicated to serving its community. Through its comprehensive range of services, professional staff, and commitment to justice, the court continues to fulfill its vital role in the Pennsylvania judicial system.

Frequently Asked Questions

  1. What are the court's regular business hours? The court operates Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 12:00 PM and 12:45 PM to 4:00 PM.
  2. How can I locate the Court Administrator's Office? Take the elevator to the third floor, turn right, go through the glass doors, and the office will be on your left.
  3. Who are the current judges serving the court? The Honorable Aaron L. Gingrich serves as President Judge, alongside Judge Jonathan W. Reed.
  4. Is there an online system for jury services? Yes, the court utilizes an eJury system for efficient jury management.
  5. How does the court accommodate individuals with disabilities? The court maintains full ADA compliance and has a specific Title II policy to ensure accessibility for all visitors.
